transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. It's very nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... well, I hope I'm in the right place. It’s really nothing major, I don't want to make a big fuss out of it, but... it's just a little thing I've been noticing lately. I help out down at the museum—just to keep busy, you know—and sometimes the folks there will be talking right to me, maybe about the next art walk or something. And I’ll be looking right at them, but then... I kind of realize I completely missed the middle of what they just said. 

I end up having to ask them to run it by me again. I feel a bit foolish about it, honestly, because I don't want them to think I'm being rude or ignoring them. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
When this happens, does it feel like you didn’t hear the words clearly?

Oh, no, no, it's not my hearing at all. I actually hear them loud and clear. 

It's more like... well, the sound goes in just fine, but my mind just takes a little detour for a second, and I don't quite process what they meant. I hope that doesn't sound too silly. I just wouldn't want you to think I'm going deaf or anything like that, because my ears work perfectly fine. I'm trying to explain it the best I can... is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
When this happens, are you usually worrying about something else?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I really don't want to give you the wrong impression—I'm not a nervous sort of person at all. Thankfully, at my age, things are pretty peaceful. I don't have a lot of big worries stressing me out or anything like that. 

When my mind wanders off like I was saying, it's... well, it's usually just drifting to nothing in particular. Just silly little everyday things, or sometimes nothing at all. I'm definitely not sitting there agonizing over problems, I promise you that. 

Does that help clear it up? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information, doctor.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. I have a very nice life, really. My wife and I are doing just fine, and I enjoy my time at the museum. 

I'm generally a pretty cheerful fellow, you know? I don't feel sad or blue or anything like that. I really hope I'm not making it sound like I'm a miserable person, because I'm truly not. I'm just a bit... well, a bit scatterbrained sometimes, I suppose. I hope that's alright to say? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.
Have you been forgetting recent conversations or appointments?

Oh, no, I don't think so. My memory is actually still pretty sharp, thankfully. I make sure to write all my appointments down on a little calendar in the kitchen, so I'm always right on time. I'd just hate to keep anyone waiting or be an inconvenience, you know? 

And as for conversations... well, as long as I caught what we were talking about in the first place, I remember it just fine. I really hope that doesn't sound defensive at all! I just want to reassure you that my memory itself is working alright, it's just that little drifting thing I mentioned before. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's the sort of detail you're looking for.
Have you had any trouble managing your finances?

Oh, no, no trouble there at all. My wife and I, well, we keep a very close eye on the checkbook. I always make sure the bills are paid right on time... I'd just hate to fall behind and cause a mess, you know? 

It's very important to me to be responsible with our money, especially now that I'm not working. I hope that shows I'm still keeping things together pretty well? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, doctor, and that I'm answering everything correctly for you.
Have you had any strokes, head injuries, or other neurologic illnesses?

Oh, goodness, no. I've been very lucky with my health, really. No strokes or... or head injuries, nothing like that at all. I try to be very careful, you know, not taking any silly risks. And I haven't had any sort of brain illnesses either, thankfully. 

I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers here? I just want to reassure you that physically, everything is perfectly fine up there. I hope that helps you rule out any of the scary stuff for your notes.
Aside from these moments of drifting, have you had any trouble using familiar appliances or technology, like the TV remote or a phone?

Oh, no, nothing like that. I can still work the TV and my phone just fine. I mean, they keep changing how everything works these days, but I manage to keep up! I'd hate to be one of those older folks who constantly needs help just to change the channel, you know? 

So no, no trouble with the remote or the phone or the microwave. Everything like that is perfectly normal. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can figure out what's going on.
Compared with a few years ago, do you feel your ability to pay attention has gotten worse?

Oh, I wouldn't say it's gotten worse, no. I mean, maybe just the normal amount that happens to anyone as they get a little older, right? It's nothing drastic. I can still sit and read the paper or listen to my wife when she's talking to me. 

I just... well, sometimes my mind wanders a tiny bit, but I really don't think it's any worse than it was a few years ago. I try very hard to stay sharp. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I'd hate for you to think I'm just letting myself go or anything like that.
